text: Shakespeare had already undergone this trial of duration. He outlived his rivals and his patrons; and a century and a half, bringing with it shifting taste, new manners, and new rules of writing, had passed over his works without diminishing the delight they afforded. Johnson gathers the whole result into a single image (Johnson 1765): "The stream of time, which is continually washing the dissoluble fabricks of other poets, passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare."
